{{nihongo|'''Noma Shrine'''|野間神社 (今治市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iyo Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ayahayatama-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakayao-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Noma-hime-no-Mikoto}}

There are multiple theories about the enshrined deities, but these four are currently treated as the shrine's deities.

Ayahayatama-no-Mikoto is the deity of {{ill|Hayatani Shrine|abstract|Q11639721|ja|速谷神社|no|Hayatani-helligdommen|simple|Hayatani Shrine|tok|tomo sewi Kajatani|qid=Q11639721}} and ancestor of the {{ill|provincial governors of Aki|Q21654103|qid=Q21654103|lt=provincial governors of Aki}}. Wakayao-no-Mikoto is his third-generation descendant and ancestor of the {{ill|Nukata-no-kuni-no-miyatsuko|Q21654103|qid=Q21654103}}. Noma-hime-no-Mikoto is regarded as Wakayao-no-Mikoto's wife.

Because Noma Shrine was called "Noma Tennō-gami" and "Nōman Tennō-gami," there is also a theory that its deity was {{ill|Gozu Tennō|de|Gozu-Tennō|it|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|zh|牛頭天王|qid=Q11570247}}, with {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} as principal deity. However, ''Noma Jinja-shi'' considers Ayahayatama-no-Mikoto, Wakayao-no-Mikoto, and Noma-hime-no-Mikoto to be the main deities, and Susanoo-no-Mikoto to have been an associated deity. That there was a medieval period when {{ill|Gozu Tennō|de|Gozu-Tennō|it|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|zh|牛頭天王|qid=Q11570247}} was enshrined is clear from documents remaining at the temple-bettō {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jōzen-ji}}.

== Origins ==
Its founding is unknown, but it is believed to have begun when Wakayao-no-Mikoto, who became {{ill|Nukata-no-kuni-no-miyatsuko|Q21654103|qid=Q21654103}}, worshiped his ancestor {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ayahayatama-no-Mikoto}}. In the ''{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi: Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi}}'', Wakayao-no-Mikoto is said to have been appointed provincial governor in the reign of {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}.

According to shrine tradition, a shrine building was constructed in {{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}}（{{ill|Taihō (era)|ca|Taiho|de|Taihō (Ära)|es|Taihō (era)|fa|تایهو (دوره)|fr|Ère Taihō|ia|Taiho|id|Taihō|ja|大宝 (日本)|ko|다이호|pt|Taihō (era)|ru|Тайхо (нэнго)|simple|Taihō (era)|sr|Таихо (ера)|th|ไทโฮ (ศักราช)|tr|Taihō (dönem)|uk|Тайхо (ненґо)|zh|大宝 (日本)|zh_yue|大寶 (日本)|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} 1）. In {{ill|766|Q30564|qid=Q30564}}（{{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|Q1373181|qid=Q1373181}} 2）, it was granted Junior Fifth Rank, Lower and given two households of shrine serfs. In {{ill|837|Q25093|qid=Q25093}}（{{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 4）, together with {{ill|Ōyamazumi Shrine|Q703904|qid=Q703904}}, it received myōjin status for the first time in the {{ill|Nankaidō|Q1376747|qid=Q1376747}} region. In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, it is listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, and in {{ill|940|Q23830|qid=Q23830}}（{{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 3）, due to prayers against pirate raiding, it was promoted to Senior Second Rank.

In the medieval period it was strongly revered by military leaders, especially the {{ill|Kōno clan|Q11554232|qid=Q11554232}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it served as a {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|ar|رقصة المطر|bg|Призоваване на дъжд|ca|Dansa de la pluja|da|Regnmageri|de|Regenmacherritual|el|Χορός της βροχής|eo|Pluvdancado|es|Danza de la lluvia|eu|Euri-dantza|fa|رقص باران (آیین)|fi|Sadetanssi|fr|Danse de la pluie|he|ריקוד גשם|hr|Ples za prizivanje kiše|hu|Esőtánc|id|Tari hujan|it|Danza della pioggia|ja|雨乞い|ko|기우제|lt|Lietaus šokis|nl|Regendans|pt|Dança da chuva|ro|Dansul ploii|ru|Обряд вызывания дождя|scn|Abballata di l'acqua di celu|simple|Rain dance|sv|Regndans|tg|Боронхоҳӣ|th|การขอฝน|tr|Yağmur yağdırma|trv|Waya lmawa quyux|uk|Обряд викликання дощу|vi|Cầu mưa|wuu|祈雨舞|zh|祈雨舞|qid=Q477738|lt=rain-prayer site}} for the {{ill|Iyo-Matsuyama Domain|Q1042087|qid=Q1042087|lt=Matsuyama domain of Iyo}}.

In 1871（Meiji 4）it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in 1895（Meiji 28）it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

== Shrine name ==
In sources such as the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}, it appears as "Noma-no-kami"; in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}, as "Noma Tennō-gami"; and in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, as "Noma Shrine." The writing of "Noma" also included characters such as 乃万, 濃満, and 濃万, deriving from {{ill|Noma District, Ehime|ja|野間郡|zh|野間郡|qid=Q266830}}（{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|qid=Q133833194}}'s {{ill|Nukata-no-kuni|Q21654103|qid=Q21654103|lt=Nukata-no-kuni}}）. In the Kenchō-era documents it appears as "Nomangu," and in Kōfuku-ji's solicited-deity register as "Shōichii Nōman Tennō-gami." There are also examples such as "Daibonten'ō-gū" and "Nomasha Daibonten'ō-gū."

Among local people it was called "Tennō-sha" or "Tennō-gū," and popularly known as "Tennon-san."

== Annual festival ==
At the annual grand festival held on May 3, dedicatory performances include the Urayasu dance, daimyo procession, lion dance, mikoshi procession, and hemp-plain sacred boat. Among these, the {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} is designated an {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Ehime|af|Ehime-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Ehime|ar|إهيمه (محافظة)|az|Ehime
